title: Offline glaucoma AI on a smartphone fundus camera tested in a prospective clinic cohort
summary: In 213 consecutive patients at a tertiary glaucoma clinic, a deep learning glaucoma system running offline on a smartphone-based fundus camera detected referral-warranted glaucoma versus no glaucoma with 92.02% accuracy, 91.36% sensitivity (95% CI 85.93-95.19) and 94.12% specificity (95% CI 83.76-98.77) against specialist diagnosis. The AI was developed previously, the study is single-center, and the no-glaucoma group is small (n=51).
ai_technology: Previously developed offline deep learning glaucoma detection system applied to disc-centered fundus images from a portable camera

evidence.tested: Prospective consecutive cohort against specialist diagnosis using clinical assessment, visual fields and SD-OCT.
evidence.unknown: Performance in screening settings outside a tertiary clinic and among glaucoma suspects; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Flags referral-warranted glaucoma from smartphone fundus images.

source_review.scope: Abstract read from Europe PMC metadata for this DOI; author affiliations from Europe PMC or Crossref. Full text not accessed.
